questions.question: How is the negative of a vector A (denoted as -A) defined relative to the original vector A?

options.text: A vector with the same magnitude as A but pointing in the exact opposite direction
A vector with a magnitude equal to the reciprocal of A pointing in the same direction
A vector perpendicular to A with zero magnitude
A vector with half the magnitude of A pointing in the opposite direction

questions.explanation: The negative of a vector A is defined as a vector that possesses the exact same magnitude as vector A but points in the opposite direction (-A).

questions.question: What is the defining characteristic of a unit vector in vector algebra?

options.text: It has a magnitude of zero and points toward the origin.
It has a magnitude of exactly 1 unit with no physical units and specifies direction.
It is always parallel to the position vector of an object.
It represents the vector sum of two perpendicular forces.

questions.explanation: A unit vector is a dimensionless vector with a magnitude of unit length (exactly 1) used specifically to indicate direction in coordinate space.

questions.question: In the Parallelogram Law of vector addition, how are two vectors geometrically arranged to find their resultant?

options.text: Head-to-tail, with the resultant connecting the tail of the first to the head of the second
Tail-to-tail, with the diagonal drawn from their common origin representing the resultant
Head-to-head, with the resultant formed by the perpendicular bisector
Parallel to each other, with the resultant equal to their scalar product

questions.explanation: According to the Parallelogram Law, two vectors are joined tail-to-tail to form adjacent sides of a parallelogram, and the diagonal drawn from their common tail represents their resultant vector.

questions.question: How is the scalar (dot) product of two vectors A and B separated by an angle θ mathematically defined?
questions.explanation: The dot product of two vectors A and B is a scalar quantity defined by A · B = A B cos θ, where θ is the angle between the vectors when placed tail-to-tail.

questions.question: What is the value of the scalar product A · B when vectors A and B are perpendicular (orthogonal) to each other?
questions.explanation: For orthogonal vectors, the angle between them is θ = 90°. Since cos 90° = 0, the scalar product A · B = A B cos 90° = 0.

questions.question: A displacement vector is given as S = 60 km, 20° South of East. What is the negative of this vector (-S)?
questions.explanation: The negative of a vector keeps the same magnitude (60 km) but reverses its direction completely. The opposite of 20° South of East is 20° North of West.

questions.question: An ant walks 40 cm due South and then 30 cm due West. What is the magnitude and direction of the ant's net displacement from its initial position?
questions.explanation: Using Pythagoras' theorem: S = √(40² + 30²) = √(1600 + 900) = √2500 = 50 cm. The direction angle is tan θ = opposite / adjacent = 30 / 40 = 0.75, which gives θ ≈ 37° West of South.

questions.question: A force vector F of magnitude 50.0 N acts at an angle of 60° above the positive x-axis. What are the horizontal (Fx) and vertical (Fy) components of this force?
questions.explanation: Horizontal component Fx = F cos 60° = 50.0 N × 0.5 = 25.0 N. Vertical component Fy = F sin 60° = 50.0 N × (√3/2) ≈ 43.3 N.

questions.question: Given a force vector F = (6i - 8j) N, what is the unit vector u_F pointing along the direction of F?
questions.explanation: Magnitude of F is |F| = √(6² + (-8)²) = √(36 + 64) = 10 N. The unit vector along F is u_F = F / |F| = (6i - 8j) / 10 = 0.6i - 0.8j.

questions.question: Vector A = 3i - 2j and vector B = 4i + 5j. What is the scalar (dot) product A · B?
questions.explanation: Using component form for dot product: A · B = Ax Bx + Ay By = (3)(4) + (-2)(5) = 12 - 10 = 2.

questions.question: A constant force F = (20i - 15j) N acts on a particle, moving it through a displacement S = (4i + 2j) m. How much work W = F · S is done by the force?
questions.explanation: Work W = F · S = Fx Sx + Fy Sy = (20 N)(4 m) + (-15 N)(2 m) = 80 J - 30 J = 50 J.

questions.question: Two vectors A and B have equal magnitudes of 10.0 units. Vector A lies along the positive x-axis, while vector B makes an angle of 60° above the positive x-axis. What is the magnitude of their resultant vector R = A + B?
questions.explanation: Resolving into components: Ax = 10.0, Ay = 0. Bx = 10.0 cos 60° = 5.0, By = 10.0 sin 60° = 8.66. Summing components: Rx = 10.0 + 5.0 = 15.0, Ry = 8.66. Magnitude R = √(Rx² + Ry²) = √(15.0² + 8.66²) = √(225 + 75) = √300 ≈ 17.3 units (or 10√3).

questions.question: An unknown vector D is added to vector C = -4i + 5j such that the resultant R = C + D has components Rx = -1 and Ry = 1. What is the magnitude of vector D?
questions.explanation: From R = C + D: Rx = Cx + Dx ⇒ -1 = -4 + Dx ⇒ Dx = 3. Ry = Cy + Dy ⇒ 1 = 5 + Dy ⇒ Dy = -4. Vector D = 3i - 4j. Magnitude |D| = √(3² + (-4)²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5.0 units.

questions.question: Vector A = i + j and vector B = -2i + 3j. What is the angle θ between vectors A and B? (Given: cos 78.7° ≈ 0.196)
A machine applies a force F = (50i + 30j) N to pull a heavy crate, causing it to move with a steady velocity v = (3i + 4j) m/s. What is the instantaneous power P delivered by the machine?
questions.explanation: Instantaneous power is the dot product of force and velocity: P = F · v = Fx vx + Fy vy = (50 N)(3 m/s) + (30 N)(4 m/s) = 150 W + 120 W = 270 W.
